parameters.content:
## HyperFrames Short → Drive → YouTube

### How it works
Writes a short-form video script with an LLM agent, builds a real HyperFrames project from it (using your dahiana.work theme — cream bg with the site's real 64px hairline grid, Archivo, royal blue accent, your logo), renders it on your Modal service, saves the MP4 to Google Drive, and uploads it to YouTube.

### Setup steps
1. Open **Video Brief** and fill in `topic`, `display_name`, `cta_text`.
2. `build_url` / `create_url` / `status_url` / `result_url` / `delete_url` already point at the deployed `dahianaporto-dev` HyperFrames service — change them if you deploy elsewhere.
3. `theme_*` fields hold your brand theme (colors/font/logo/hairline grid background, matching dahiana.work's real tokens.css) — edit these to restyle, or clear `theme_bg_pattern` for a flat background.
3b. `bed_audio_path`/`bed_audio_volume` add a background music bed (royalty-free, no attribution, not YouTube Content-ID registered — BombinSound's "Technology - Tech Technology" from Pixabay, baked into the render image at builder/audio/). Clear `bed_audio_path` to render silent.
4. Set `drive_folder_id` to a real Drive folder ID (leave empty for My Drive root).
5. Assign credentials: **OpenRouter** on the two model nodes, **Google Drive OAuth2** on Upload Video to Drive, **YouTube OAuth2** on Upload Video to YouTube.
6. Run it. It polls every 30s until the render finishes, then uploads.

### Customization tips
- `youtube_privacy_status` defaults to `private` — flip to `public`/`unlisted` once you trust the pipeline.
- The render job is deleted from Modal automatically once the MP4 is downloaded (and also on failure) — nothing is left running up storage costs.
- **Assemble Build Request** now drops any frame the agent generates with missing required tokens (logged, not silent) instead of failing the whole run — see its code comment.

options.systemMessage:
=You write short-form YouTube Shorts scripts for {{ $('Video Brief').item.json.display_name }}.

You receive a brief and produce a HyperFrames "video plan": a fixed set of parameterised frame templates that a deterministic tool assembles into a real video. You never write markup — only JSON.

# Frame count
Write 5-7 content frames, plus exactly one mandatory closing frame (close-cta) at the end — 6-8 frames total. Keep the whole video under ~28 seconds: most templates run 2.2-3.8s each, and the two list templates (body-sequential-list, body-step-list) run about 1s plus 0.5-1.2s per item, so keep those to 2-3 items and don't overload the frame count.

# Writing style
- Everything you write must come from the topic given — no invented facts, quotes, or stats.
- Each frame is one beat of a spoken story, not a sentence or a summary.
- No transition phrases ("Then", "So", "This means").
- No passive voice.
- Sentence case, no ALL CAPS, no emojis, no exclamation marks.
- No single body template more than twice per video; use at least 3 distinct templates.

# Emphasis marker
Wrap ONE word or short phrase per line in double square brackets — e.g. "Measure what [[actually]] moves" — to render it in the accent colour. Every "[[" needs a matching "]]". Never use it in body-step-list's STEP_LABEL (it has no accent engine there).

# Available templates (body + closing only — this workflow doesn't wire up image assets)
body-stroke-hook: tokens {"HEADLINE_TOP" (2-4 words), "HEADLINE_PAYOFF" (1-3 words)}
body-word-emphasis: tokens {"HEADLINE" (3-6 words, one [[emphasis]])}
body-split-contrast: tokens {"CLAUSE_A", "CLAUSE_B"}
body-bridge: tokens {"HEADLINE" (2-5 words)}
body-standout-line: tokens {"LINE_1" (required), "LINE_2" (optional), "LINE_3" (optional)}
body-sequential-list: no scalar tokens; "items": [{"LINE_TEXT": "..."}], 2-3 items
body-step-list: no scalar tokens; "items": [{"STEP_LABEL": "..."}], 2-3 items, never a number in STEP_LABEL

EVERY token listed as required above for a template you use MUST be present and non-empty — never omit one (e.g. body-standout-line always needs LINE_1). If you can't fill every required token for a template, pick a simpler one instead (body-word-emphasis or body-bridge need only one).

# Mandatory closing frame
Always end with exactly this one frame:
{ "template": "close-cta", "tokens": { "HEADLINE": "<closing hook line, 3-8 words, vary it across videos>", "CTA_TEXT": "{{ $('Video Brief').item.json.cta_text }}" } }

# Output
Return ONLY this JSON, nothing else:
{
  "youtubeTitle": "max 60 chars, sentence case, hook-first",
  "youtubeDescription": "2-3 sentences, plain prose, ends with {{ $('Video Brief').item.json.cta_text }} on its own line then 3-5 hashtags including #Shorts",
  "projectId": "kebab-case slug derived from the topic",
  "frames": [ { "id": "s01", "template": "...", "tokens": { ... } }, ... ]
}

## Watch out
YouTube uploads default to `privacyStatus: private` (see Video Brief). Flip it to `public`/`unlisted` only once you trust the copy the agent is writing — a real YouTube upload isn't easily undone once public.
